name: MCP Server
description: Turns Jellyfin into an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server so AI assistants such as Claude can work with your media in plain language. Ask what to watch next, search movies, shows and music, check what was recently added or what you watched last week, start or pause playback on any of your devices, manage playlists, favorites and watched status, and, as an administrator, run scheduled tasks and library scans. 22 tools in four scopes (library, playback, manage, admin). Every access token belongs to one Jellyfin user and only sees what that user can see. Create tokens on the plugin settings page and connect your assistant to https://your-server/mcp.
overview: Let AI assistants like Claude search your library, control playback and manage playlists.

versions.changelog: Tokens can be limited to chosen libraries: pick them when creating a token on the settings page. A restricted token only sees items in those libraries (playlists and collections show only their entries from them) and cannot have the admin scope. Existing tokens keep access to every library.

MCP prompts: movie_night, catch_me_up, whats_new and library_health (administrators only) show up in clients as slash commands and follow the token's scopes. jellyfin_recently_added items now include dateAdded.

Audio and subtitle tracks: new jellyfin_get_media_tracks; jellyfin_play can start with a chosen audio and subtitle track and jellyfin_playback_control can switch them during playback (set_audio_track, set_subtitle_track). New read-only admin tools, for administrators only: jellyfin_server_status (version, pending restart, activity, disk space), jellyfin_list_all_sessions (every user's sessions, with transcoding details) and jellyfin_activity_log.

Adds three read-only library tools: jellyfin_similar_items (more like a movie, series, album or artist), jellyfin_movie_recommendations (personal recommendations grouped by reason) and jellyfin_list_collections (your collections, or those containing an item).

Tools return structuredContent with a declared outputSchema, and every tool has a display title. Adds MCP protocol revision 2026-07-28 (stateless, with server/discover) next to 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18 and 2025-03-26. Validates the Origin header on /mcp, with a new "Allowed origins" setting for browser-based clients. Server instructions explain how the tools fit together. Breaking: jellyfin_list_tasks, jellyfin_list_users, jellyfin_list_libraries and jellyfin_list_sessions now return { "items": [...] } instead of a bare array.
